claims.text: The stress-strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr can be explained by the combined effects of thermal expansion mismatch and mechanical loading.
The thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr can be explained by the combined effects of thermal expansion mismatch and mechanical loading.
Thermal expansion mismatch induces internal stresses in the alloy.
Mechanical loading contributes to internal stresses in the alloy.
The induced internal stresses alter the alloy's microstructure.
Microstructural state affects mechanical properties such as strength and ductility in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy system.
Combined thermal and mechanical loading will change the alloy's strength relative to separate thermal or mechanical loading.
Combined thermal and mechanical loading will change the alloy's ductility relative to separate thermal or mechanical loading.
Combined thermal and mechanical loading will change the alloy's elastic moduli relative to separate thermal or mechanical loading.
The relevant behavior extends to temperatures as high as 1250 °C.
The initial material is polycrystalline and may contain varying amounts of cold work and aging.
Separate thermal and mechanical loading conditions provide the baseline for the controlled comparison.
Neutron diffraction, digital image correlation, and finite-element modeling can be combined to test the proposed internal-stress mechanism.
Stress-strain curves, thermal expansion coefficients, elastic moduli, and microstructural evolution are the proposed response variables.
The magnitude and direction of the proposed effects are uncertain.
Finding no significant effect of thermal expansion mismatch and mechanical loading on stress-strain or thermoelastic behavior would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as combined thermal and mechanical loading but lists cold rolling and aging, which are respectively mechanical-only and thermal-only treatments; these overlap with the stated baseline of separate thermal and mechanical loading.
